full_text_en:
Jiangsu Province Wuxi City People's Procuratorate v. Shanghai Yangpu District Greening and City Appearance Administration Bureau et al. — environmental civil public interest litigation

**Case Summary**

In environmental civil public interest litigation initiated by a procuratorial authority as a public interest litigant, the judicial review requirements for withdrawal of the lawsuit are different from those for ordinary civil cases. On the basis of clarifying the equality of status of both parties in environmental civil public interest litigation cases and reiterating that the polluter bears the responsibility for environmental restoration, the review standards for granting permission to withdraw the lawsuit should be stricter. In terms of substantive review, the standard of "all claims have been realized" should include that the ecological environment has been fully restored and that there is no risk of future continued environmental pollution and ecological damage. In terms of procedural review, local procuratorial authorities at all levels shall fulfill corresponding review and approval procedures when withdrawing a lawsuit; withdrawal of a lawsuit approved by the Supreme People's Procuratorate and determined by the people's court through substantive review to meet the withdrawal standards shall be permitted.

Public interest litigant: Jiangsu Province Wuxi City People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Shanghai Yangpu District Greening and City Appearance Administration Bureau, domiciled at Shuangyang Road, Yangpu District, Shanghai.
Legal representative: Xu Feng, Director of the Bureau.

Defendant: Shanghai Yangpu Environment Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Pingliang Road, Yangpu District, Shanghai.
Legal representative: Hu Bo, General Manager of the Company.

Defendant: Shanghai Chengdi Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at Chenhai Highway, Chongming District, Shanghai.
Legal representative: Gu Jianmin.

Defendant: Xu Guoqiang, male, Han ethnicity, born March 2, 1962, residing in Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Xu Biao, male, Han ethnicity, born July 8, 1970, residing in Wujiang District, Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Cui Mingrong, male, Han ethnicity, born March 17, 1964, residing in Lujiang County, Hefei City, Anhui Province.

Defendant: Xu Jinfa, male, Han ethnicity, born September 26, 1963, residing in Huishan District, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province.

The public interest litigant, Jiangsu Province Wuxi City People's Procuratorate (hereinafter referred to as Wuxi Procuratorate), filed an environmental civil public interest litigation lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as Wuxi Intermediate People's Court) against the defendants Shanghai Yangpu District Greening and City Appearance Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Yangpu City Appearance Bureau), Shanghai Yangpu Environment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huanfa Company), Shanghai Chengdi Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chengdi Company), Xu Guoqiang, Xu Biao, Cui Mingrong, and Xu Jinfa.

The public interest litigant, Wuxi Procuratorate, alleged: Starting from 2013, the defendant Yangpu City Appearance Bureau entrusted part of its domestic waste to the defendant Xu Guoqiang for disposal. Xu Guoqiang entered into a disposal contract in the name of the defendant Chengdi Company. In March 2015, Xu Guoqiang turned over the domestic waste to the defendant Xu Biao and his fleet for disposal. Xu Biao, through the defendants Cui Mingrong and Xu Jinfa, dumped the waste on the riverbank near Luoshe Town, Huishan District, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province, causing severe pollution to the surrounding ecological environment. After the pollution incident occurred, the People's Government of Huishan District, Wuxi City (hereinafter referred to as Huishan District Government) promptly organized relevant departments to carry out emergency response and disposal of the dumped domestic waste. On December 2, 2016, the Xishan District People's Court of Wuxi City (hereinafter referred to as Xishan Court) convicted Xu Guoqiang, Xu Biao, Xu Jinfa, and Cui Mingrong of the crime of environmental pollution and imposed corresponding criminal penalties. Subsequently, during the performance of its duties, the Wuxi Procuratorate discovered that the actions of the seven defendants, including Yangpu City Appearance Bureau, had damaged the environmental public interest. Upon verification with the Wuxi Civil Affairs Bureau, among the existing environmental protection social organization legal persons in the city that meet the conditions stipulated in Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law of the PRC, the social organizations are the Wuxi Environmental Protection Industry Association and the Wuxi Happy Volunteer Environmental Protection Association. The Wuxi Procuratorate consulted the above social organizations in writing, and both stated that they were unwilling to initiate environmental civil public interest litigation in this case. Therefore, the Wuxi Procuratorate, as the public interest litigant, filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting judgment that: Yangpu City Appearance Bureau, Huanfa Company, Chengdi Company, Xu Guoqiang, Xu Biao, Cui Mingrong, and Xu Jinfa jointly and severally bear the following costs: 1. Emergency response costs of RMB 1,460,179.16 incurred from the illegal transportation and disposal of domestic waste; 2. Costs of RMB 150,000 for formulating the environmental restoration plan; 3. Ecological environment restoration costs of RMB 425,320 (calculated based on the estimated amount in the restoration plan, subject to actual occurrence); 4. Costs for monitoring, supervision, and other expenses to be incurred by the environmental protection authority of Wuxi for subsequent implementation of ecological environment restoration (subject to actual occurrence). During the trial of this case, the ecological environment restoration project was implemented, and monitoring and expert demonstrations were conducted. The Wuxi Procuratorate clarified the amounts for its claims 3 and 4 as: ecological environment restoration costs of RMB 476,070, subsequent monitoring and supervision costs of RMB 3,000, and expert demonstration costs of RMB 5,400.

The defendant Yangpu City Appearance Bureau argued: This incident serves as a warning that it must effectively strengthen environmental protection awareness in its management work, further enhance regulatory responsibilities, and raise the level of comprehensive management of various types of waste. It has taken a series of corrective measures to strictly prevent the recurrence of such incidents, and has actively urged the relevant responsible parties to fulfill their legal obligations as soon as possible, bear the necessary costs, cooperate with relevant departments to complete environmental restoration work, and fully realize the claims of the public interest litigant.

The defendant Xu Guoqiang argued: Willing to bear all consequences arising from his wrongful actions and fully cooperate with the environmental restoration work.

The defendants Huanfa Company, Chengdi Company, Xu Biao, Cui Mingrong, and Xu Jinfa did not submit defenses.

The Intermediate People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province found at first instance:

**I. Facts Regarding the Illegal Dumping and Landfilling of Domestic Waste by Defendants Xu Guoqiang, et al.**

Starting from 2013, the defendant Xu Guoqiang, in the name of the defendant Chengdi Company, entered into a contract for the transportation and disposal of domestic waste with the defendant Yangpu City Appearance Bureau. During this period, the defendant Huanfa Company provided transshipment services for the domestic waste involved at Pier No. 2, Jungong Road, Shanghai. In March 2015, Xu Guoqiang, knowing that the defendant Xu Biao did not have the qualification to transport and dispose of domestic waste, turned over part of the domestic waste to Xu Biao for outward transportation and disposal by fleet. Xu Biao then contacted the defendant Cui Mingrong to find a landfill site. Cui Mingrong contacted the defendant Xu Jinfa, and they designated the riverbank area along Zhihugang in Huaqi Village, Luoshe Town, Huishan District, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province as the landfill site, and built a road and a makeshift dock in that section of the river for dumping and landfilling waste. In May 2015, Xu Guoqiang illegally disposed of six shiploads of domestic waste totaling 2,360.74 tons through Xu Biao; actually disposed of four shiploads totaling 1,670 tons, while two shiploads totaling 690.74 tons were not dumped because they were discovered by local residents; and illegally profited over RMB 20,000. Xu Biao illegally disposed of eight shiploads of domestic waste totaling 3,387.09 tons (of which two shiploads of 1,026.35 tons came from other sources); actually disposed of four shiploads totaling 1,670 tons, while four shiploads totaling 1,717.09 tons were not dumped because they were discovered by local residents; and illegally profited over RMB 30,000. Cui Mingrong and Xu Jinfa actually disposed of six shiploads of domestic waste totaling 2,400 tons; Cui Mingrong illegally profited over RMB 50,000, and Xu Jinfa illegally profited RMB 9,000. The above domestic waste was all dumped at the Zhihugang section of Huaqi Village, Luoshe Town, Huishan District, Wuxi City.

**II. Facts Regarding Emergency Response by Wuxi Environmental Protection Authorities to the Domestic Waste Involved**

1. In May 2015, the dumping and landfilling of domestic waste by defendants Xu Guoqiang, et al., was exposed following a report. The Huishan District Environmental Protection Bureau of Wuxi City (hereinafter referred to as Huishan EPB) commissioned Shanghai Huace Pinbiao Testing Technology Co., Ltd. to test the domestic waste involved. The test results showed that the solid waste in the garbage contained heavy metals lead, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, and metalloid arsenic, and the leachate contained chromium heavy metals, all of which are toxic substances.

2. To promptly eliminate the environmental pollution caused by the above domestic waste to the surrounding water bodies and soil, the Huishan District Government organized relevant departments to carry out emergency response to the domestic waste illegally dumped in the Zhihugang river section. Huishan EPB commissioned the Jiangsu Provincial Environmental Engineering Consulting Center to prepare the "Emergency Response Plan for the Illegal Dumping and Landfilling Incident of Foreign Solid Waste (Municipal Domestic Waste) in the Luoshe Section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, Huishan District, Wuxi City" and, in accordance with this plan, carried out emergency removal, disposal, and monitoring of the dumped waste and leachate on site, as well as the four shiploads of waste and leachate that were attempted to be illegally dumped but not actually dumped.

3. In December 2015, Huishan EPB commissioned the Jiangsu Provincial Ecological Environment Assessment Center to assess the losses and costs during the emergency response phase of the environmental pollution incident involved. The Center issued the "Assessment Report on Losses and Costs During the Emergency Response Phase of the Illegal Dumping and Landfilling Incident of Foreign Solid Waste (Municipal Domestic Waste) in the Luoshe Section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, Huishan District, Wuxi City." The report specified that, based on construction contracts, work completion certificates, and existing receipts, etc., the total losses and costs during the emergency response phase amounted to RMB 2,054,270.65, mainly including: emergency removal and disposal costs for the dumped waste and leachate on site of RMB 1,032,581.67; emergency removal and disposal costs for the four shiploads of waste and leachate that were attempted to be illegally dumped but not actually dumped of RMB 568,633.98; emergency monitoring costs of RMB 93,055; and costs for the preparation of the emergency response plan, environmental damage assessment costs, etc.

4. In July 2016, commissioned by Huishan EPB, Wuxi Qingda Architectural Design and Research Institute Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wuxi Qingda Institute) issued the "Environmental Restoration Technical Plan for the Illegal Dumping and Landfilling Incident of Foreign Solid Waste (Municipal Domestic Waste) in the Luoshe Section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, Huishan District, Wuxi City" (hereinafter referred to as the "Environmental Restoration Technical Plan"), estimating subsequent restoration costs at RMB 607,600.

Because part of the domestic waste involved did not come from defendants Xu Guoqiang and Xu Biao, the Wuxi Procuratorate, based on the proportion of waste volume, discretionarily fixed the emergency response costs arising from the illegal transportation and disposal of domestic waste at RMB 1,460,179.16.

**III. Facts Regarding the Criminal Liability of Defendants Xu Guoqiang, et al., for Environmental Pollution**

On December 2, 2016, the Xishan District People's Court of Wuxi City (hereinafter referred to as Xishan Court) issued Criminal Judgment No. (2016) Xifa Huanxing Chuzi No. 00001, finding that the defendants Xu Guoqiang, Xu Biao, Cui Mingrong, and Xu Jinfa jointly dumped toxic substances, causing severe environmental pollution, and constituted the crime of environmental pollution. The court sentenced: Xu Guoqiang to one year and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000; Xu Biao to one year and nine months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 60,000; Cui Mingrong to one year and eight months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 60,000; Xu Jinfa to one year and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000; and ordered the confiscation of illegal gains. The RMB 180,000 in environmental damage restoration fees paid by Xu Guoqiang was to be deposited into the Wuxi City Environmental Public Interest Fund special account. This criminal judgment has now taken legal effect.

**IV. Facts Regarding the Ecological Environment Restoration Involved in This Case During the Trial**

1. After accepting this case, the court publicly announced the acceptance of the case in accordance with the law and notified the People's Government of Yangpu District, Shanghai and the Shanghai Municipal Greening and City Appearance Administration Bureau. During the announcement period, no social organization entitled to bring a lawsuit applied to participate in the proceedings.

2. During the trial of this case, the court commissioned the Huishan District Environmental Monitoring Station of Wuxi City (hereinafter referred to as Huishan Monitoring Station) to monitor the current environmental status of the polluted area involved. The "Monitoring Report" [(2017) Huanjian (Shui) Zi No. (041)] showed that water bodies in the polluted area involved had local exceedances of COD (chemical oxygen demand).

3. The court selected three experts from the "Wuxi Court Environmental Resources Judicial Protection Expert Database," including from the School of Environment and Civil Engineering of Jiangnan University, Wuxi Municipal Design and Research Institute Co., Ltd., and Wuxi Environmental Monitoring Central Station. These experts formed an expert group, conducted on-site investigations, and organized an expert demonstration meeting based on the "Monitoring Report" issued by Huishan Monitoring Station, conducting expert demonstrations on the previously prepared "Environmental Restoration Technical Plan." The expert group required the addition of post-restoration monitoring content. Based on the expert opinions, Wuxi Qingda Institute revised the "Environmental Restoration Technical Plan." The court publicly announced the revised "Environmental Restoration Technical Plan," during which no relevant citizens, legal persons, or other organizations raised objections.

4. Both parties selected the qualified Jiangsu Yigao Environmental Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yigao Company) to implement the environmental restoration project. After completion, Yigao Company issued the "Work Report on the Environmental Restoration Project for the Illegal Dumping and Landfilling Incident of Foreign Solid Waste (Municipal Domestic Waste) in the Luoshe Section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, Huishan District, Wuxi City" (hereinafter referred to as the "Environmental Restoration Project Report"), confirming that the environmental restoration work had been fully completed in accordance with the requirements of the "Environmental Restoration Technical Plan."

5. The court commissioned Wuxi Oasis Environmental Monitoring Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Oasis Company) to monitor the restored area. The "Monitoring Report" [(2017) Huanjian (Shui) Zi No. (D2506)] showed that the restored water bodies met Class III water quality standards.

6. The court again organized an expert demonstration meeting to conduct expert demonstrations on the "Environmental Restoration Project Report." The expert group, based on the "Monitoring Report" issued by Oasis Company, determined that the environmental restoration work had achieved the predetermined goals of the restoration plan.

**V. Facts Regarding the Defendants' Voluntary Assumption of Environmental Restoration Responsibility and the Wuxi Procuratorate's Withdrawal of the Lawsuit**

1. The total environmental losses in the polluted area involved amounted to RMB 2,094,649.16, including: emergency response costs from illegal transportation and disposal of domestic waste of RMB 1,460,179.16; costs for formulating the environmental restoration plan of RMB 150,000; ecological environment restoration costs of RMB 476,070; subsequent monitoring costs of RMB 3,000; and expert demonstration costs of RMB 5,400 [referencing the "Measures for the Administration of Expert Review Fees of Wuxi Municipal Administrative Institutions (Trial)"]. During the trial of this case, the defendant Xu Guoqiang voluntarily paid to the court RMB 2,055,499.16, representing the environmental emergency response and restoration costs claimed in the Wuxi Procuratorate's earlier claims, and requested that the previously paid environmental restoration fee of RMB 180,000 be included in this case to pay for the actual subsequent restoration costs, monitoring costs, and expert demonstration costs, and stated that, due to the holistic nature of environmental restoration, no distinction would be made as to the proportion of his participation in the dumping, and all restoration costs would be paid together. He also requested that the court directly pay the above costs to the units or individuals who had incurred the environmental restoration costs.

2. Given that the damaged ecological environment in this case had been effectively restored and the social public interest had been fully protected, with the approval of the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the public interest litigant Wuxi Procuratorate applied to the court to withdraw the lawsuit on the grounds that all claims had been realized and there was no need for further litigation.

3. The court organized a hearing, attended by deputies to the Huishan District People's Congress of Wuxi City, village representatives from the area where the polluted area was located, responsible persons from the local environmental protection and urban management departments, and environmental public interest lawyers from Wuxi. The meeting reported on the environmental restoration process. The public interest litigant Wuxi Procuratorate attended and explained the reasons for applying to withdraw the lawsuit. All attending representatives unanimously recognized that the polluted area had been effectively restored and had no objections to the Wuxi Procuratorate's withdrawal of the lawsuit.

The Intermediate People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

The "reduction, resource utilization, and harmless treatment" of municipal domestic waste are important means to achieve a circular economy society, a resource-conserving society, and an environmentally friendly society, and are one of the important symbols of a city's economic development and civilization. The removal and disposal of municipal domestic waste shall comply with the state's regulations on environmental protection and environmental sanitation management to prevent environmental pollution. Article 64 of the Environmental Protection Law of the PRC stipulates that anyone who causes damage due to environmental pollution or ecological destruction shall bear tort liability in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Tort Liability Law of the PRC. Article 65 of the Tort Liability Law of the PRC stipulates that anyone who causes harm due to environmental pollution shall bear tort liability. The defendants in this case failed to comply with the laws and regulations on the transportation and disposal of municipal domestic waste, causing environmental pollution, and shall bear tort liability.

To achieve effective supervision over the restoration of the ecological environment involved in this case, the court publicly announced the acceptance of the case in accordance with the law, notified the relevant administrative departments of the Shanghai jurisdiction, commissioned a professional institution to monitor the current status of the polluted environment, formed an expert group from the environmental resources judicial protection expert database to conduct on-site inspections, demonstrate, and revise the "Environmental Restoration Technical Plan," and publicly announced the plan. After the environmental restoration institution implemented the restoration project as agreed by both parties, the court re-commissioned a professional institution for post-restoration monitoring and again organized expert demonstrations. The monitoring results and expert opinions both indicated that the environmental restoration work had been completed. The court also invited representatives from the polluted area to attend a hearing, and all attending representatives unanimously recognized that the environment had been effectively restored. During the trial of this case, the defendant Yangpu City Appearance Bureau actively implemented corrective measures and clearly stated that it would further strengthen regulatory responsibilities to strictly prevent the recurrence of such incidents. At this point, the court found that the ecological environment of the polluted area had been restored to its pre-pollution state and the environmental restoration goals had been achieved.

Pursuant to Article 9 of the "Measures for the Pilot Work of People's Courts Trying Public Interest Litigation Initiated by People's Procuratorates" issued by the Supreme People's Court, if the people's procuratorate applies to withdraw the lawsuit before the conclusion of court debate, or if all claims of the people's procuratorate have been realized after the conclusion of court debate and it applies to withdraw the lawsuit, permission shall be granted. In this case, the Wuxi Procuratorate, based on the fact that part of the waste did not come from defendants Xu Guoqiang and Xu Biao, argued that based on the proportion of waste volume, the emergency response costs from illegal transportation and disposal of domestic waste should be fixed at RMB 1,460,179.16, which is consistent with the provisions of Article 67 of the Tort Liability Law of the PRC. During the proceedings, the costs of implementing the ecological environment restoration project (RMB 476,070), the costs of formulating the environmental restoration plan (RMB 150,000), subsequent monitoring costs (RMB 3,000), and expert demonstration costs (RMB 5,400) are all necessary costs for ecological environment restoration and for restoring the environment, and shall be borne by the polluter. The Wuxi Procuratorate's claim that the defendants should jointly bear the above total costs of RMB 2,094,649.16 is consistent with relevant legal provisions. These costs have been fully paid by the defendants. The court found that the defendants had assumed full compensation liability for the polluted area.

In summary, the ecological environment of the polluted area involved in this case had been restored, and the defendants had assumed compensation liability. All claims of the public interest litigant Wuxi Procuratorate had been realized, and its application to withdraw the lawsuit had been approved by the Supreme People's Procuratorate and had complied with the relevant approval procedures. Therefore, its application for withdrawal of the lawsuit was granted.

Accordingly, in accordance with the provisions of Article 145, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Intermediate People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province rendered a ruling on May 27, 2017:

Permission is granted for the public interest litigant, Jiangsu Province Wuxi City People's Procuratorate, to withdraw the lawsuit.
